https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c2dk.text: Image source, Getty Images Image caption, The village of Beit Jinn is southwest of Syria's capital Damascus By Henry Moore Published 22 August 2026 Syria has condemned an Israeli attack on the village of Beit Jinn, southwest of the country's capital Damascus, which officials said hit a civilian vehicle and left several people injured. The attack was the second known Israeli strike on Syria in the past week, with Syria branding it a "violation" of its sovereignty and international law. In a post on X, the Israeli military said it had targeted a "terrorist" in the "final stages" of preparing attacks which posed an immediate threat to soldiers. The latest incident comes days after reports emerged Israel had struck a military airbase close to the Turkish border, which Syria said threatened to escalate tensions in the region. After the earlier attack, Washington issued a rare rebuke of Israel, calling it an "unnecessary escalation that does not advance regional stability". In an interview on Friday, the US ambassador to Turkey, Tom Barrack, suggested that the strike could be "the Israelis baiting the Turks" in an attempt to draw Turkey into a conflict ahead of upcoming Israeli elections. Barrack's comments led Israel's far-right defence minister, Israel Katz, to describe his account as "full of inaccuracies". Writing on X, Katz added Israeli forces were acting "in light of clear intelligence information about Turkey's intentions". Following Tuesday's strikes on the Abu al-Duhur airbase, the office of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu published a statement: "Israel and Syria agreed to a status quo in security matters, which Syria was on the verge of breaching by permitting Turkish troops to deploy at an airbase near Aleppo." Image source, Anadolu via Getty Images Image caption, Abu al-Duhur military base captured by anti-Assad forces in December 2024 After the strike Turkey did not confirm whether any of its troops moved to the Abu al-Duhur airbase, which sits 70km from the Turkish border. However, Ankara rejected Israel's suggestion that it posed a threat. Abu al-Duhur airbase has been out of service as a dedicated military airfield since 2013. Rebel forces seized control of the base as they swept through the country in December 2024. Israel occupies territory in southwest Syria it seized after the fall of Bashar al-Assad in 2024. Syria has been trying to rebuild its military facilities that were damaged during the offensive that saw Bashar al-Assad's government overthrown. The Turkish military has provided assistance to Syria since the overthrow of Assad, while Israel continues to view both countries with deep suspicion. Al-Sharaa has forged closer ties with the West since coming to power, particularly the US and in November 2025 he became the first Syrian leader to visit the White House. Photograph: Kirsty Wigglesworth/PA Sarah Ferguson Sarah Ferguson to return to UK after relocating amid Epstein revelations Former Duchess of York moved to Swiss chalet during fallout over her friendship with convicted child sex offender Sammy Gecsoyler Sat 29 Aug 2026 10.32 EDT First published on Sat 29 Aug 2026 08.42 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Sarah Ferguson will return to the UK after relocating to a Swiss chalet amid the fallout over the friendship between her and her ex-husband, Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor , and the convicted child sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, according to reports. The pair were stripped of their royal titles in October over the scandal of their relationship with Epstein. According to the Sun, the former Duchess of York, 66, is renting a six-bedroom gated property in the home counties. Ferguson used to live with Mountbatten-Windsor at Royal Lodge in Windsor until he was forced to vacate the premises and move to Marsh Farm on King Charles’s Sandringham estate in Norfolk. She could “imminently” move into a new home, which has three bathrooms and a “granny annexe”, according to the Sun. It is believed Ferguson has been spending time out of the public eye at a Swiss chalet in Verbier since leaving Royal Lodge, and her belongings were collected from Andrew’s home in Sandringham this week, the newspaper added. Her expected return comes just days after the Duke and Duchess of Sussex arrived back in the UK with their children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet. The family are expected to enjoy an “extended stay” in Britain, with the children enrolled at school and due to start next week. There is clearly trouble ahead for Harry and Meghan on their return to the UK. One email exchange suggested Ferguson had taken her daughters to see Epstein in the US days after he was released from prison for child sex crimes. A year after his conviction for child sex crimes, Ferguson thanked Epstein for being the “brother” she had “always wished for” in an email. Last September, the Mail on Sunday published emails from 2011, in which Ferguson privately described Epstein as her “supreme friend” and apologised for “letting him down”, despite having publicly called her association with him “a gigantic error of judgment”. The messages were sent less than two months after she had insisted she would “never have anything to do with [Epstein] again”, amid pressure over the ties she and Mountbatten-Windsor had maintained with him – including a £15,000 payment Epstein made to help settle Ferguson’s debts. Epstein has been the downfall of Mountbatten-Windsor, who was stripped of his titles by the King because of “serious lapses of judgment” over his friendship with the late child sex offender. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to First Edition Our morning email breaks down the key stories of the day, telling you what’s happening and why it matters after newsletter promotion Ferguson lost her courtesy royal divorcee title and reverted to her original name, and also lost the freedom of the city of York after councillors voted unanimously to remove the honour over her links to Epstein. She and Mountbatten-Windsor were given the honour as a wedding present from York in 1987 during a visit to the city. The former duchess has published more than 50 books – largely children’s titles – but after the Epstein revelations, thousands of copies of her latest children’s book were withdrawn from sale and “pulped”. Earlier this year, Ferguson’s international charity, Sarah’s Trust, announced its closure “for the foreseeable future”. Seven charities, including the Teenage Cancer Trust and children’s hospice, have also cut ties and revoked Ferguson’s patronage due to her links with Epstein. Six companies linked to Ferguson – S Phoenix Events, Fergie’s Farm, La Luna Investments, Solamoon Ltd, Philanthrapreneur Ltd and Planet Partners Productions Ltd – were wound down in February after more damaging revelations came to light with the release of the Epstein files. ΔΤ/ ΔΕΣΦΑ DESFA CEO: Vertical Corridor moving from political ambition to implementation Share: Share via Facebook Share via Twitter Share via LinkedIn Share via Email Share via WhatsApp Copy Link Προσθέστε την «Ν» ως προτιμώμενη πηγή στο Google Hellenic Gas Transmission System Operator DESFA participated in the 2nd Quadrilateral Ministerial Meeting on Energy and Connectivity, held in Belgrade with the participation of Greece, Serbia, Bulgaria and North Macedonia, highlighting progress on the Vertical Gas Corridor and its key role in turning Greece’s strategic position and natural gas infrastructure into a gateway for diversified and competitive sources of supply to Southeast and Central Europe. DESFA CEO Maria Sferruzza met with the energy ministers and the heads of natural gas and electricity transmission system operators from the four countries, underscoring DESFA’s commitment to moving the Vertical Corridor from political cooperation to implementation, with a focus on infrastructure, available capacity, operational coordination and, ultimately, reliable gas flows across the region. As DESFA said in a statement, a key step is the extension of the Vertical Corridor to North Macedonia and Serbia, following the Memorandum of Understanding signed in Thessaloniki in September. This will create an additional northern route for flows entering through Greece and strengthen connectivity with the Western Balkans and markets further north. The Serbia-North Macedonia gas interconnector will be linked to the Greece-North Macedonia Interconnector (IGNM), which is currently under construction. The Greek section is expected to be completed by the end of 2026, while the North Macedonian section is expected to be completed in 2027. According to DESFA, Greece is already emerging as a key southern entry point for diversified natural gas supplies to the region. Through DESFA’s transmission infrastructure and LNG facilities, including the Revithoussa LNG terminal, together with the Alexandroupolis FSRU, the Greek system provides access to multiple gas sources and greater flexibility for northbound flows. For DESFA, the next phase involves operating this infrastructure as an integrated regional system. Together with gas transmission system operators across the region, DESFA is working to identify available routes and capacity, address remaining bottlenecks and assess targeted investments where needed, making the most efficient use of existing infrastructure while strengthening commercial and regulatory coordination along the Corridor. According to DESFA, this practical approach is particularly important as Europe prepares for the gradual phase-out of Russian natural gas. Greece and the wider Southeast and Central European region are preparing for the 2026/27 winter with a clear focus on resilience. While the evolving supply environment requires continued vigilance, diversified sources, additional infrastructure and stronger regional coordination provide the flexibility needed to manage the transition and support secure and competitive natural gas supplies. DESFA CEO: Vertical Corridor moving from political ambition to implementation DESFA CEO Maria Sferruzza said: “The Vertical Corridor is moving from political ambition to implementation. The infrastructure and capacity already available across our region provide a strong foundation, but the priority now is to make use of this capacity — connecting systems, removing bottlenecks and enabling reliable and competitive flows. The extension of the Corridor to North Macedonia and Serbia, also following the Memorandum of Understanding signed in Thessaloniki in September, is an important step in this direction. As the southern gateway of the Corridor, DESFA has a clear role to play, connecting diversified sources of supply entering through Greece with the markets of Southeast and Central Europe and the Western Balkans.
